title: Non-surgical tibia fracture treatment
description: Non-surgical tibia fracture treatment is an outpatient procedure where your doctor treats your broken shinbone (tibia) without surgery. Your doctor will take X-rays to determine the fracture type and severity. If the break is stable and properly aligned, surgery may not be necessary. You'll wear a cast or walking boot to immobilize your shin and allow healing. You'll need to avoid weight-bearing or only partially bear weight as directed for several weeks, using crutches if necessary. Ice and elevation help manage swelling and pain. Periodic X-rays monitor healing progress. Physical therapy helps restore your strength and motion once healing is underway. Full healing typically takes 8-16 weeks depending on fracture severity and location. Some tibia fractures may need the bones manipulated into proper position before casting. The cost of this procedure may vary depending on whether your doctor needs to manually reposition (manipulate) the bone fragments into proper alignment, or whether the fracture can heal in its current position without manipulation.
